evidence: Cic. Clod. et Cur. 5: tū fēstīvus, tū ēlegāns, tū sōlus urbānus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In early Latin it meant fastidious, over-refined (Lewis & Short); classically, refined and tasteful.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 309.
